cause.claim_level: reproduced and attributed by a kernel-level test plus generated 32-bit machine code; not a hypothesis
cause.statement: tree_step.c begin_body copied the caller's intercept point and face normal into the query, and finish copied them out, with float assignments. gcc -m32 (x87 math by default) compiles each as an flds/fstps pair; loading a signalling NaN into the x87 register quietens it (0x7fa00001 becomes 0x7fe00001). x86_64 uses SSE moves and keeps the payload. Signed zero and subnormals are unaffected by an x87 copy; only a signalling NaN is changed, which is why only that word differed.

attribution.kernel_level_red: diag1-kernel-words-i686: the new trees.rs test (reinterprets whole arrays, never calls f32::from_bits) FAILS on i686 with the unchanged C kernel: the C copy is sufficient to cause the failure.
attribution.c_only_fix: diag2-c-only-fix-i686: with ONLY the C change, both the kernel-level test and the existing tree_host test pass. The Rust f32::from_bits/to_bits conversions in tree_host.rs did NOT change the word in this i686 debug profile, so no Rust production change is made; the existing host test keeps exercising that conversion.

repair.tree_step.c: begin_body copies the caller's intercept point and face normal into the query with memcpy of their twelve bytes each; finish copies the answer out with memcpy; a compile-time check pins sizeof(vec3d) == 3 * sizeof(float). Position copies, the arithmetic and the intersection helpers (which write computed floats before the hit decision) are unchanged.
repair.trees.rs: tests only: two reinterpret helpers and run_words, and a_miss_gives_the_callers_point_and_normal_back_bit_for_bit_whatever_they_hold. No production Rust changed.
repair.word_contract: a no-hit query returns every caller output word bit-exact: signalling NaN payload and sign, quiet NaN payload, signed zero, subnormals, the largest finite values. A miss that partly overwrote the buffers still returns what the helpers wrote. Hit geometry still comes from the existing kernel; the raw output words are never adopted as campaign/physical state.
repair.order_contract: unchanged and asserted by the existing host test: terrain at the old end, then the new end, each only if inside the map; no fast path bypasses a required terrain call (the new kernel test also asserts two lookups on every exit it covers).
repair.fp_rng_identity: no change to the FP guard, rounding, arithmetic, tie rules, identity or any RNG; the new test covers three miss exits (altitude above the tree height, a range under 0.1 m, an empty sector) with three raw-word cases each.
